name: CPGRAMS (Centralized Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System)
managing_body: Department of Administrative Reforms & Public Grievances (DARPG), Government of India
domain: Public Service Delivery (Central Ministries/Departments & States/UTs)

offline_channels: By post or hand to DARPG

languages_supported: English + 22 Eighth Schedule languages (via BHASHINI) with voice-based utility
categories: Central Board of Direct Taxes (Income Tax)
Railways, Pensions (pgportal.gov.in/pension/), and other Central/State Departments

fees.offline_csc: CSC service fee applies only when filed through a Common Service Centre

sla_and_timelines.interim_reply_rule: If resolution exceeds 21 days, an interim Action Taken Report (ATR) must be issued.

mandatory_pre_steps: File one clear issue per grievance.
Government employees must exhaust prescribed internal departmental channels first.
exclusions: RTI matters
Court-related or sub-judice matters
Religious matters
Personal and family disputes
Matters impacting territorial integrity or friendly foreign relations
Complaints sent via email are not entertained
documents_required: Complainant name, address, mobile number, and email
Application, transaction, or service reference number
Chronological event dates and previous complaint numbers
Supporting receipts, letters, or screenshots converted to PDF

upload_constraints.notes: Verify current max file size and character limit live on portal before upload.

step_by_step_guide: Register once at pgportal.gov.in/Registration with name, address, mobile number, and email.
Sign in via OTP or password (or via UMANG / MyGrievance app).
Select Lodge Public Grievance, choose the relevant Central Ministry/Department or State, describe one specific issue and desired remedy, and attach supporting PDF.
Submit and save the unique Registration Number.
Track status at pgportal.gov.in/status and review the Action Taken Report (ATR).
Rate the disposal; selecting 'Poor' enables the Appeal option within 30 days.
escalation_path: Rate disposal 'Poor' -> File Appeal to Nodal Appellate Authority (resolved within 30 days). Closed grievances cannot be reopened; lodge a fresh grievance citing the closed reference if needed.

automation.g2g_api_note: API integration exists only for 17 States/UTs, 4 Central Ministries, and UMANG.
automation.recommended_handoff: Generate structured complaint text and consolidated PDF packet + copy-paste field tray.

name: National Consumer Helpline (NCH / INGRAM)
managing_body: Department of Consumer Affairs, Government of India
domain: Consumer Goods & Services (Informal Pre-Litigation Mediation)

contact_channels.helpline_hours: 8:00 AM to 8:00 PM, 7 days a week (except national holidays), with call-back facility

sla_and_timelines.nature: Facilitative mediation via ~1,038 Convergence Partner companies
sla_and_timelines.limitation_warning: Filing on NCH does NOT pause the statutory 2-year limitation clock for formal Consumer Commissions.

mandatory_pre_steps: Raise a complaint with the seller/platform's customer care or Grievance Officer first and keep the ticket number.
exclusions: Cannot pass legally binding orders or award punitive damages (non-adjudicatory)
documents_required: Invoice, bill, or receipt showing amount paid
Photo of MRP / defective product (if applicable)
Warranty card or service agreement
Prior complaint ticket number and company correspondence

upload_constraints.notes: Supporting documents can also be uploaded post-registration using Docket Number at consumerhelpline.gov.in/user/upload-docs.php.

step_by_step_guide: Register on consumerhelpline.gov.in (or message WhatsApp 8800001915 / call 1915).
Select sector, company (Convergence Partner if listed), and grievance type.
Enter purchase/order details, amount paid, and brief summary of the issue.
Upload bill/invoice and support correspondence to receive a Docket Number.
Monitor company response online; escalate to e-Jagriti if unresolved.
escalation_path: Unresolved NCH grievance -> Send 15-day written/legal notice -> File formal Consumer Complaint on e-Jagriti (or Legal Metrology department for MRP violations).

automation.recommended_handoff: Launch pre-populated WhatsApp chat to 8800001915 or provide Docket upload checklist.

name: e-Jagriti (Unified Consumer Commission Portal — Replaced e-Daakhil)
managing_body: Department of Consumer Affairs / NCDRC, Government of India
domain: Formal Consumer Litigation (Refund, Replacement, Compensation)

urls.deprecated_url: Retired on 1 January 2025; do not use. Replaced by e-Jagriti.

languages_supported: Multilingual interface with voice-to-text, chatbot, and virtual hearings (also usable by NRIs)
categories: Deficiency in service (e-commerce, travel, education, telecom, medical, banking/insurance)
Unfair trade practices & overcharging above MRP

eligibility_and_thresholds.pecuniary_jurisdiction_basis: Value of goods or services actually PAID (consideration), NOT compensation claimed
eligibility_and_thresholds.territorial_jurisdiction: Where complainant resides/works, where opposite party operates, or where cause of action arose

slabs_by_consideration_paid.range: Above INR 5 lakh to INR 10 lakh
Above INR 10 lakh to INR 20 lakh
Above INR 20 lakh to INR 50 lakh
Above INR 50 lakh to INR 1 crore
Above INR 1 crore to INR 2 crore

slabs_by_consideration_paid.fee_inr: Higher bands up to INR 7,500 ceiling

mandatory_pre_steps: Complain in writing to the seller/company first.
Recommended: Try NCH (1915) and send a 15-day written demand/legal notice via Registered Speed Post + email.
exclusions: Large-scale commercial purchases (for resale/commercial profit)
Do not track consumer cases on regular eCourts (use e-Jagriti or Confonet instead)
documents_required: Government Photo ID (Aadhaar, PAN, or Driving Licence)
Index
Proforma for filing complaint
Synopsis with chronological List of Dates & Events
Memo of Parties (exact registered legal name & address of opposite party from invoice)
Drafted Consumer Complaint (facts, jurisdiction, limitation paragraph, relief sought, verification)
Notarised Affidavit (missing affidavit or Memo of Parties is the top rejection cause)
Vakalatnama (ONLY if represented by an advocate)
Annexures: invoice/bill, payment proof, warranty/agreement, defect photos, chat/email trail, prior legal notice

upload_constraints.notes: Practitioner accounts note limits around ~10 files of a few MB each; combine and compress annexures clearly (e.g., 'Annexure C-3 service job card').

step_by_step_guide: Sign up at e-jagriti.gov.in with mobile/email 6-digit OTP and upload ID proof.
Click 'File New Case' -> 'Consumer Complaint'.
Enter amount paid, claim value, cause-of-action date, state/district, category/subcategory, and optional priority flags (senior citizen, widow, differently abled, serious illness).
Enter complainant and opposite party details.
Upload the mandatory legal set (Index, Proforma, Synopsis, Memo of Parties, Complaint, Notarised Affidavit) plus annexures.
Select Commission, tick declaration, and carefully review Preview (no edits allowed after final submission).
Submit, save the Reference Number, and pay fee via Dashboard -> Payment History if value paid exceeds INR 5 lakh.
Cure any registry scrutiny objections online and attend physical or virtual hearings.
escalation_path: District Commission -> State Commission -> NCDRC -> Supreme Court (within 30 days under Sec 67 for NCDRC original orders).

automation.recommended_handoff: Auto-generate downloadable PDFs for Index, Proforma, Synopsis, Memo of Parties, Draft Complaint, and Affidavit template + pre-submission validator.

name: National Cybercrime Reporting Portal (NCRP) & 1930 Helpline
managing_body: Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), Ministry of Home Affairs
domain: Cyber Financial Fraud, Hacking & Online Harassment
jurisdiction: Pan-India (auto-routed to State Police Cyber Cell)
categories: Online Financial Fraud (UPI, card, net banking, fake investment/task/job scams)
Online and Social Media Related Crime (impersonation, cyberbullying, blackmail, threats)
Report Crime Related to Women/Child (anonymous reporting available)

sla_and_timelines.financial_fraud_golden_hour: Call 1930 immediately (within minutes/24 hrs) to trigger inter-bank fund freeze
sla_and_timelines.bank_zero_liability_window: Report unauthorized third-party breach to bank within 3 working days (shadow credit within 10 working days)
sla_and_timelines.physical_fir_escalation_trigger: If no response within 7-10 days or loss exceeds INR 1 lakh

mandatory_pre_steps: For financial fraud: Call 1930 FIRST and notify your bank within the same hour (phone + written) to block cards/UPI—do not delay to collect documents.
exclusions: Portal acknowledgement does NOT automatically guarantee an FIR has been registered; police process per procedure.
Anonymous option is NOT available for financial fraud or general cybercrime (only Women/Child route).
documents_required: Government Photo ID (Aadhaar, PAN, Passport, or Driving Licence) and Address Proof
Bank name, last 4 digits of account/card, exact amount, date and time
UTR / UPI transaction reference numbers and bank debit SMS/statements
Fraudster's phone number, UPI ID, bank account, website URL, or social media handle
Exported full chat logs (WhatsApp/Telegram/Instagram), timestamped screenshots, and full email headers
1930 acknowledgement number and bank complaint reference number
step_by_step_guide: If money was debited: Call 1930 immediately with bank, amount, time, UTR, and recipient details.
Call your bank's official helpline in the same hour, block compromised credentials, and get a written complaint reference.
Go to cybercrime.gov.in -> File a Complaint -> accept terms -> choose 'Report Cyber Crime' (or Women/Child route).
Register with State, name, and mobile OTP.
Select category/subcategory, enter chronological incident description (200+ characters), money trail, and suspect details.
Upload clearly named screenshots, statements, and chat exports; submit and save the Acknowledgement Number.
Track status on cybercrime.gov.in; carry printout to local Cyber Crime Police Station for formal FIR if stalled after 7-10 days or loss > INR 1 lakh.
escalation_path: 1930 + Bank alert -> cybercrime.gov.in -> Physical FIR at Cyber Crime Police Station -> RBI CMS (cms.rbi.org.in) if bank violates RBI limited-liability circular after 30 days.

automation.recommended_handoff: Emergency Golden-Hour screen with one-tap tel:1930, bank zero-liability email generator, and structured evidence packager.

name: RBI Complaint Management System (CMS — Integrated Ombudsman Scheme)
managing_body: Reserve Bank of India (RB-IOS)
domain: Banks, NBFCs, Digital Lenders, UPI/Wallets & Credit Bureaus (CIBIL/Experian)
categories: Commercial / Co-operative Bank service deficiencies & unauthorized transactions
NBFC & digital lender grievances (recovery agent harassment, hidden charges, KFS mismatch)
Payment system disputes (UPI, PPI wallet, prepaid card, mobile banking failures)
Credit Information Company disputes (wrong CIBIL / Experian reporting)

sla_and_timelines.filing_limitation: Within 1 year of lender's reply (or 1 year + 30 days if no reply)

mandatory_pre_steps: MANDATORY: Submit a written complaint to the bank, NBFC, payment operator, or CIC first and wait for an unsatisfactory reply OR 30 days of silence. Skipping this causes automatic rejection as 'Non-maintainable'.
exclusions: Complaints filed without completing the 30-day lender pre-step
Entities not regulated by RBI
documents_required: Copy of written complaint submitted to the bank/NBFC/CIC with date
Lender's reply (if received) or proof of 30 days elapsed
KYC ID proof
Transaction proofs, statements, loan KFS, or CIBIL report screenshots
step_by_step_guide: Complete the mandatory 30-day written pre-step with your bank/NBFC/CIC.
Visit cms.rbi.org.in and click 'File a Complaint'.
Select entity category (Bank / NBFC / System Participant / CIC) and the specific regulated entity.
Verify your mobile number via OTP (becomes your permanent tracking login).
Enter personal, transaction, and relief-sought details and upload evidence (max 10 MB total).
Submit and save the Complaint Registration Number (CRN) received via SMS/email.
escalation_path: Bank/NBFC Internal Grievance -> Principal Nodal Officer -> RBI Ombudsman (cms.rbi.org.in; binding award if accepted by complainant) -> Consumer Commission (e-Jagriti) or Civil Court.

automation.recommended_handoff: Generate Step-1 written lender complaint email + start 30-day countdown reminder + auto-compress evidence under 10 MB.

name: SEBI SCORES 2.0 (SEBI Complaints Redress System)
managing_body: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
domain: Stock Brokers, Mutual Funds, Listed Companies, Depositories & RTAs
categories: Listed companies / Registrar & Transfer Agents (unpaid dividends, share transfer delays)
Stock brokers & stock exchanges (unauthorized trades, payout delays)

sla_and_timelines.limitation_period: 1 year from cause of action per SEBI official investor portal (some broker guides note 3 years; enforce stricter 1-year rule)

mandatory_pre_steps: Lodge complaint with the broker, listed company, or intermediary first and keep its ticket/reply.
exclusions: Investment losses caused by market price movement
Unregistered advisors or unregulated app-based schemes
Matters pending before a court or tribunal
Disputes purely between two investors
Anonymous complaints or market intelligence tips (send market-law violation tips to mi.sebi.gov.in)
documents_required: PAN card (mandatory KYC validation)
Mobile number and email address
Contract notes, demat/mutual fund statements, and prior correspondence with entity

upload_constraints.notes: Supporting PDF attachment (legacy documentation cites 1 MB cap; keep files compact and check portal prompt).

step_by_step_guide: Register on scores.sebi.gov.in (or SEBISCORES app) with PAN, mobile OTP, and email.
Log in, select 'Register Complaint', pick category and regulated entity name.
Enter transaction date, factual description, and relief sought, and upload supporting documents.
Submit to get a unique Complaint Registration Number; entity must respond within 21 calendar days.
If dissatisfied, request First Review (Designated Body) and, if still unresolved, Second Review (SEBI).
escalation_path: Entity -> SCORES 2.0 (21 days) -> Designated Body 1st Review -> SEBI 2nd Review -> SMART ODR -> Securities Appellate Tribunal (SAT) / Consumer or Civil Court.

automation.recommended_handoff: Pre-step broker complaint email template + 21-day SLA tracker + review-stage checklist.

name: IRDAI Bima Bharosa & Insurance Ombudsman (CIO)
managing_body: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) & Council for Insurance Ombudsmen
domain: Life, Health, Motor & General Insurance Claim Rejections / Servicing

urls.bima_bharosa_verification_note: Verify live link via irdai.gov.in before routing; live automated check returned unexpected content on this subdomain.

contact_channels.helpline_hours: 8:00 AM to 8:00 PM, Monday to Saturday
contact_channels.offline_address: Policyholders Protection & Grievance Redressal Dept, IRDAI, Sy. No. 115/1, Financial District, Nanakramguda, Gachibowli, Hyderabad – 500032

categories: Rejected or partially settled health/life/motor claims
Claim settlement delays or unjustified deductions
Policy servicing, mis-selling, or hidden charges

eligibility_and_thresholds.who_can_file: Insured person or claimant only (third-party advocates/agents alone generally not entertained by IRDAI cell)

fees.online: Free (INR 0) for Insurer GRO, Bima Bharosa, and Insurance Ombudsman

sla_and_timelines.insurer_gro_resolution_days: 14 to 15 days (wait up to 30 days before Insurance Ombudsman)
sla_and_timelines.ombudsman_filing_limitation: Within 1 year of insurer rejection or 1 year from insurer failing to reply within 30 days

mandatory_pre_steps: Submit a written grievance to the insurer's Grievance Redressal Officer (GRO) first and retain the written acknowledgement and date.
exclusions: Insurance Ombudsman cannot hear disputes already pending in a Consumer Commission, civil court, or arbitration
Ombudsman claim limit is INR 50 lakh (including expenses)
documents_required: Policy schedule / certificate of insurance and claim number
Itemized hospital bills or vehicle repair estimates
Insurer's rejection / partial settlement / deduction letter
Written complaint to insurer GRO, acknowledgement, and TPA/insurer email trail
step_by_step_guide: Lodge a written grievance with your insurer's GRO (find email at irdai.gov.in/list-of-gros) and wait 14-15 days.
If unresolved, register on Bima Bharosa (verify live link from irdai.gov.in) or email complaints@irdai.gov.in / call 155255.
Upload supporting PDFs/images (keep filenames under 24 characters and total size under 10 MB) and verify via OTP.
If unresolved after 30 days from initial insurer complaint (and claim <= INR 50 lakh), file free online at cioins.co.in/Complaint/Online.
Participate in Ombudsman mediation; if unresolved, Ombudsman passes an award binding on the insurer.
escalation_path: Insurer GRO (15 days) -> IRDAI Bima Bharosa -> Insurance Ombudsman (cioins.co.in, up to INR 50L) -> Consumer Commission (e-Jagriti) or Civil Court (complainant retains right to escalate even after Ombudsman award).

automation.recommended_handoff: Auto-rename uploaded files <= 24 chars, draft GRO email, track 15-day / 30-day clocks, and provide mailto/CIO handoff.

name: MahaRERA (Maharashtra Real Estate Regulatory Authority)
managing_body: Government of Maharashtra (State RERA model applies across other states)
domain: Homebuyer vs. Builder / Real Estate Agent Disputes

contact_channels.offline_address: Mumbai Division Office: 501, Express Building, 14-E Road, Churchgate, Mumbai – 400020

categories: Delay in possession / refund with statutory interest (Section 18)
Structural or workmanship defects within 5 years of possession (Section 14)
Unauthorized alteration of sanctioned plans without allottee consent (Section 14)
Refusal to furnish sanctioned plans or schedules (Section 19)

fees.conciliation_forum: INR 1,000 + GST (payable once opposite party consents within 7 days)

sla_and_timelines.advisory_observed_timeline_months: 8 to 14 months for formal contested hearings

mandatory_pre_steps: Confirm the project is registered on maharera.maharashtra.gov.in and note its MahaRERA Registration Number (e.g., P51700XXXXXX).
Mirror all developer communications via email or Registered Speed Post (verbal/WhatsApp promises are weak evidence alone).
exclusions: Unregistered real estate projects
Tenant vs. landlord rental deposit disputes (route to Small Causes Court / Competent Authority instead)
Forum exclusivity warning: Check before filing simultaneously in both RERA and Consumer Court for the same relief
documents_required: MahaRERA Project Registration Number
Copy of registered Agreement for Sale (or Allotment Letter if unregistered)
Consolidated PDF of payment receipts and bank statements
Chronological written correspondence / demand letters with builder
Complainant PAN / Aadhaar
step_by_step_guide: Search and verify the project's MahaRERA registration number at maharera.maharashtra.gov.in.
Register as a Citizen user at maharerait.mahaonline.gov.in using email and mobile OTP.
Choose either MahaRERA Conciliation Forum (INR 1,000 + GST, faster amicable settlement) OR Online Complaint Filing (Form A for Authority / Form B for Adjudicating Officer).
Select Division (e.g., Pune), enter project registration number, complaint type, and statutory section (e.g., Sec 18).
Upload Agreement for Sale, payment receipts, and dated correspondence PDF.
Pay INR 5,000 online, submit, and track hearing dates via your Complaint Number.
escalation_path: Demand Letter -> MahaRERA Conciliation (INR 1,000+GST) -> MahaRERA Formal Complaint (Form A/B, INR 5,000) -> MahaRERA Appellate Tribunal (Form C within 60 days) -> Bombay High Court (substantial question of law).

automation.recommended_handoff: Project-ID checker prompt + demand letter PDF generator + chronological evidence binder.

name: SAMADHAN Portal (Central Labour Dispute Portal)
managing_body: Ministry of Labour & Employment / Central Industrial Relations Machinery (CIRM)
domain: Unpaid Wages, Illegal Termination, Gratuity, Bonus & Industrial Disputes (Central Sphere)
jurisdiction: Pan-India (Central Sphere establishments handled by CIRM Regional Labour Commissioners)
categories: Delay in payment of wages / unauthorized deductions
Non-payment of Minimum Wage or Overtime allowance
Industrial disputes, charter of demands, and general labour complaints

sla_and_timelines.process: Conciliation notice issued by RLC/CIRM officer; referred to Labour Court/Tribunal if conciliation fails

mandatory_pre_steps: Send a formal 7-to-15-day written Demand Notice to the employer detailing gross/net unpaid salary and exact months due.
exclusions: Local private shops, startups, and state-sphere factories generally fall under the State Labour Commissioner (e.g., Mahakamgar in Maharashtra) rather than Central CIRM.
documents_required: Aadhaar-linked mobile number
Appointment/offer letter and increment letters
Last 6 months' payslips and bank statements
Attendance logs / work emails / Slack proof
HR admission of pending dues (emails/messages) and 7-day Demand Notice
Brief Statement of Claim and employer registered address + HR/Director name
step_by_step_guide: Visit samadhan.labour.gov.in (or open SAMADHAN inside UMANG app) and register as 'Worker' using Aadhaar-linked mobile OTP.
Select 'Raise Dispute' and pick the relevant dispute category (e.g., Non-payment of wages).
Enter employer company details, registered address, and HR/Director contact.
Upload your Demand Notice, appointment letter, payslips, and Statement of Claim.
Submit to generate a Case ID and attend conciliation hearings scheduled by the Regional Labour Commissioner.
escalation_path: 7-Day Demand Notice -> SAMADHAN / RLC Conciliation (Form-H settlement) -> Labour Court / CGIT adjudication (or Civil Summary Suit under Order 37 CPC within 3 years for senior/managerial recovery).

automation.recommended_handoff: Auto-draft 7-day Demand Notice & Statement of Claim PDF + Central vs. State sphere jurisdiction router.

name: Mahakamgar (Maharashtra Department of Labour)
managing_body: Commissioner of Labour, Government of Maharashtra
domain: Unpaid Wages, Shops & Establishments, Gratuity & Factory Labour Disputes (State Sphere)
jurisdiction: Maharashtra (with Pune Division ALC/GLO & 15 Worker Facility Centers)

helpline: 020-25542611 (Pune Division Addl. Commissioner — verify via pune.gov.in)
contact_channels.offline_pune_anchor: Addl. Commissioner of Labour, Pune: Bungalow No. 5, Mumbai-Pune Road, Shivajinagar, Pune – 411005; Pune City WFC: Inaam Nagar, Tadiwala Rd (9970765491)

categories: Unpaid salary / FnF settlement (State-sphere private companies, shops, establishments)
Wrongful termination without notice pay / statutory severance
Minimum wages, working hours, and Maharashtra Shops & Establishments violations
Delayed Gratuity (Form N before Controlling Authority/ALC; 10% p.a. statutory interest if delayed >30 days)

eligibility_and_thresholds.wage_ceiling_note: Payment of Wages Act authority historically applied to wages up to INR 24,000/month; managerial/higher-salary recovery typically proceeds via Civil Summary Suit (Order 37 CPC, 3-year limitation). Note Maharashtra is transitioning to the four consolidated Labour Codes (2025-2026 rules).

mandatory_pre_steps: Send a 7-to-15-day written Demand Notice to employer/HR specifying unpaid months and exact dues.
documents_required: Appointment/offer letter or employment proof (emails/chats)
Last 6 months' payslips and bank account statements
Attendance records / work communication proof
Copy of written Demand Notice sent to employer
step_by_step_guide: Send a formal 7-15 day Demand Notice to your employer.
Log in or register on mahakamgar.maharashtra.gov.in (solving CAPTCHA) to lodge a state-sphere labour complaint.
Alternatively, visit your area Assistant Commissioner of Labour (ALC), Government Labour Officer (GLO), or taluka Worker Facility Center listed on pune.gov.in.
Attend conciliation / inspection; if employer refuses settlement, seek referral to Labour Court or file Civil Summary Suit (Order 37 CPC).
escalation_path: Demand Notice -> Mahakamgar / Area ALC Conciliation -> Labour Court / Civil Summary Suit (Order 37 CPC) + NALSA Free Legal Aid (all industrial workmen qualify regardless of income).

automation.recommended_handoff: 7-day Demand Notice generator + Pune area-to-ALC/WFC lookup + NALSA workman eligibility banner.

name: SHe-Box (Sexual Harassment Electronic Box)
managing_body: Ministry of Women & Child Development, Government of India
domain: Sexual Harassment at Workplace (POSH Act, 2013)
jurisdiction: Pan-India (Central Govt, State Govt, Private Sector, Organized & Unorganized)
categories: Demand or request for sexual favours
Implied or explicit promise of preferential treatment or threat of detrimental treatment/employment status
Humiliating treatment likely to affect health or safety
Unwelcome physical, verbal, or non-verbal conduct of a sexual nature
exclusions: Strictly for sexual harassment at the workplace under the POSH Act, 2013; false/malicious complaints attract statutory penalty under Section 14 and Rule 10.
documents_required: Complainant contact and work status details
Workplace name, district, office address, and Nodal/Contact person details
Respondent name, designation, email, and working relationship
Brief incident narrative (max 500 words) and supporting evidence (emails, chats, screenshots)
step_by_step_guide: Open shebox.wcd.gov.in (or Mission Shakti App) and click 'Register your Complaint'.
Read and accept the POSH Act Section 14 / Rule 10 statutory declaration.
Complete the 4-step form: (1) Complainant details, (2) Workplace details (Central/State/Private), (3) Respondent details, (4) Incident details & IC status.
Write description (<=500 words) and attach supporting file (<=2 MB PDF/JPEG/PNG).
Submit; the portal directly forwards the complaint to the jurisdictional Internal Committee (IC) or Local Committee (LC) Nodal Officer and provides a tracking status.
escalation_path: SHe-Box -> Internal Committee (IC) / District Local Committee (LC) -> Police / Criminal complaint (for physical assault/stalking) + NALSA Free Legal Aid (all women qualify regardless of income).

automation.recommended_handoff: Private 500-word incident draft helper (stored locally only) + 2 MB evidence compressor + direct deep link.

name: EPFiGMS (EPF i-Grievance Management System)
managing_body: Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO)
domain: Provident Fund Withdrawal, KYC, Transfer & EPS Pension Grievances
categories: PF Member grievances (withdrawal/claim settlement delay, transfer, KYC mismatch, non-deposit by employer)
EPS Pensioner grievances (PPO / monthly pension issues)
documents_required: UAN (Universal Account Number), PPO Number (pensioners), or Establishment Number
Supporting documents (claim receipt, passbook screenshot, payslips showing PF deduction)
step_by_step_guide: Visit epfigms.gov.in/grievance/grievancemaster (or UMANG -> EPFO Services).
Select Status (PF Member, EPS Pensioner, Employer, or Others).
Enter UAN / PPO number (auto-maps your concerned EPFO field office) and verify via OTP.
Select PF account(s), grievance category, describe the issue, and upload supporting document(s).
Submit to get a unique Registration Number via SMS & email; send reminders or feedback online.
escalation_path: EPFiGMS -> Reminder on EPFiGMS -> CPGRAMS (Ministry of Labour & Employment).

automation.recommended_handoff: UAN checklist + direct deep link to epfigms.gov.in/grievance/grievancemaster.

name: Aaple Sarkar Grievance Redressal Portal (Maharashtra)
managing_body: Chief Minister's Office & Directorate of Information Technology, Government of Maharashtra
domain: State Departments, District/Taluka Offices & Municipal Escalations
categories: District Level grievances (Collector, Tehsil/Taluka, Zilla Parishad, Municipal escalation)
Scholarship / DBT grievances (handled separately on mahadbt.maharashtra.gov.in)
documents_required: Mobile number and email for OTP
Full name, district, taluka, and address
Concerned department name, dates, and prior local complaint number (if escalating)
Supporting photos or PDF

upload_constraints.mahadbt_grievance_portal_only: JPEG/JPG/PDF strictly between 15 KB and 256 KB

step_by_step_guide: Register at grievances.maharashtra.gov.in/en/citizens/verify using mobile and email OTP.
Log in and click 'File a Grievance'.
Choose Administration Type: 'District Level' (local/civic/taluka) or 'Mantralaya Level' (state department).
Select District, Taluka, Department, and Subject, describe facts clearly, and upload evidence.
Submit to generate a Grievance Token Number (SMS & email).
Track status; if resolution within 21 working days is unsatisfactory, mark 'Dissatisfied' to escalate to higher authority.
escalation_path: Municipal / Local Office -> Aaple Sarkar (21 working days) -> Mark 'Dissatisfied' for higher-authority escalation -> RTI Act Section 6(1) for Action Taken Report.

automation.recommended_handoff: Bilingual (English/Marathi) grievance draft generator + 21-working-day SLA timer.

name: Maharashtra Police CCTNS & Pune City Police Citizen Portal
managing_body: Maharashtra Police / Pune City Police
domain: Criminal Offences, e-Complaints, Lost & Found, Missing Mobile Reports
categories: Emergency crimes & threats to personal safety (dial 112)
Lost & Found documents/items (informational report only — no police investigation)
Missing mobile phone (with IMEI blocking follow-up)

sla_and_timelines.electronic_fir_rule: Information submitted electronically for an FIR must be signed in person within 3 days to be taken on record.

exclusions: Pure civil disputes (e.g., routine landlord security deposit disputes or product defects) unless criminal cheating/fraud/assault is involved.
Pune Lost & Found portal is strictly informational (no investigation); false reporting is a punishable criminal offence.
documents_required: Government ID proof and contact mobile (for OTP)
Date, time, exact place of occurrence, and brief chronological facts
For lost mobile: IMEI number, mobile number, and telecom service provider
Supporting proof (photos, call logs, financial records for EOW/cheating)
step_by_step_guide: For immediate danger, dial 112 or 100 immediately.
For lost documents/phone in Pune, file on punepolice.gov.in/report-us/lost-and-found (or MobileMissingForm.aspx on citizen.mahapolice.gov.in) using mobile OTP.
For criminal e-Complaints, register/login on citizen.mahapolice.gov.in and submit facts.
For a formal FIR, visit the jurisdictional police station (or sign an electronically submitted FIR information within 3 days).
escalation_path: Local Police Station -> Senior Police Inspector / DCP -> Magistrate / High Court or Free Legal Aid via DLSA.

automation.recommended_handoff: Civil-vs-Criminal triage gate + one-tap tel:112 / WA prefill + written complaint PDF template.

name: PMC CARE (Pune Municipal Corporation Grievance System)
managing_body: Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC)
domain: Civic Services, Roads/Potholes, Drainage, Garbage, Water, Streetlights & Unauthorized Construction
jurisdiction: Pune Municipal Corporation limits (15 Administrative Wards; excludes PCMC)

contact_channels.helpline_note: A third-party site cites 1800-233-4040, but official pmc.gov.in pages uniformly publish 1800-103-0222.

categories: Potholes & road damage (PMC Road Mitra / PMC CARE)
Garbage collection & sanitation (PMC ISWM / PMC CARE)

sla_and_timelines.observed_third_party_estimates: Garbage: 3-7 days; Streetlights: 7-14 days; Drainage: 15-30 days; Roads/potholes: 30-90 days (actual times vary by ward).

exclusions: Does NOT cover Pimpri, Chinchwad, Akurdi, Nigdi, or Bhosari (route to PCMC instead).
PMC policy prohibits loading PMC web pages inside third-party iframes.
documents_required: Clear geotagged photograph with recognizable landmark
Road name, area, Administrative Ward (1 of 15), and streetlight pole number (if applicable)
Duration of problem and complainant mobile number
step_by_step_guide: Take a clear photo showing the defect and a nearby landmark.
File via WhatsApp (8888251001 or 9689900002), online at complaint.pmc.gov.in/home or pmccare.in/home, PMC CARE app, or Toll-Free 1800-103-0222.
Select category/subcategory, pin GPS location/ward, attach photo, and save the Complaint Ticket Number.
If closed without actual repair, reopen quoting the old ticket number, email the specific Ward Assistant Commissioner / Zone DMC, or escalate on Aaple Sarkar.
escalation_path: PMC CARE Ticket -> Ward Assistant Commissioner email & Zone DMC (Zones 1-5) -> Public nudge @PMCPune (with ticket ID, no personal phone) -> Aaple Sarkar (21 working days) -> RTI under Section 6(1).

automation.recommended_handoff: GPS point-in-polygon Ward auto-detector (via DataMeet GeoJSON) -> instant WhatsApp prefill + Ward/DMC mailto escalation.

name: Tele-Law & Nyaya Bandhu (Free Pre-Litigation Legal Advice)
managing_body: Department of Justice, Ministry of Law & Justice (DISHA Scheme) & CSC
domain: Free Pre-Litigation Legal Advice for All Citizens
categories: Family, maintenance of women, children & senior citizens

eligibility_and_thresholds.who_qualifies: ALL Indian citizens regardless of income (100% free)

documents_required: Name and mobile number (OTP)
Aadhaar / basic ID (may be requested at CSC)
Relevant dispute documents for the 20-minute lawyer call
step_by_step_guide: Sign up at tele-law.in/beneficiary/auth/signup or via the Tele-Law Mobile App (or visit nearest CSC).

name: NALSA / MSLSA / DLSA (Free Legal Aid & Lok Adalats)
managing_body: National Legal Services Authority & Maharashtra State Legal Services Authority
tier: National / State / District Legal Services Authorities
domain: Free Court Representation, Drafting, Lok Adalat & Permanent Lok Adalat

contact_channels.offline_pune_anchor: DLSA Pune & Permanent Lok Adalat, New Building, 1st Floor, District & Sessions Court Premises, Shivajinagar, Pune – 411005 (+ 35 District Legal Aid Clinics)

categories: Free advocate representation, court/process fees, drafting & certified copies (civil & criminal)
Regular / National Lok Adalats (amicable compromise; court fee refunded if pending case settles)
Permanent Lok Adalat (pre-litigation Public Utility Service disputes up to INR 1 crore)

section_12_status_exempt_no_income_cap: Members of Scheduled Caste (SC) or Scheduled Tribe (ST)
Persons with disability or mental illness
Victims of mass disaster, ethnic violence, caste atrocity, flood, drought, earthquake, or industrial disaster
eligibility_and_thresholds.section_13_genuine_case: Subject to prima facie genuine case; income affidavit is generally sufficient under Section 13(2).

permanent_lok_adalat_rules.scope: Public Utility Services only (transport, postal/telecom, power/water, public sanitation, hospital/dispensary, insurance)
permanent_lok_adalat_rules.pre_litigation_bar: Must be filed BEFORE approaching any court for the same dispute
permanent_lok_adalat_rules.binding_adjudication: If conciliation fails, PLA decides on merits under Sec 22C(8); award is final and executable as a civil decree (only Article 226/227 High Court writ review applies).

documents_required: Aadhaar card copy
Passport-size photograph
Caste certificate (if applying under SC/ST)
Income certificate or income affidavit under Section 13(2) (if applying under income category)
Brief written account of the dispute and relevant supporting papers
step_by_step_guide: Verify Section 12 eligibility (status-based or below state income ceiling—INR 3 lakh/year in Maharashtra).
Apply online via NALSA's LSMS portal (linked from nalsa.gov.in / maharashtra.nalsa.gov.in), by email, by post, or in person at DLSA Front Office (or call 15100).
Receive decision and Panel Advocate appointment letter within 7 days.
For pre-litigation Public Utility disputes (<= INR 1 crore), apply directly to the Permanent Lok Adalat at District Court before filing any court case.
escalation_path: Complaint against assigned legal aid lawyer -> Written application to assigning SLSA/DLSA or email nalsa-dla@nic.in.

automation.recommended_handoff: 15-second Section 12 Eligibility Screener + auto-drafted Legal Aid Application & Income Affidavit PDF.

name: Maharashtra Rent Control Competent Authority & Small Causes Court (Pune)
managing_body: District Judiciary / Competent Authority under Maharashtra Rent Control Act, 1999
domain: Landlord-Tenant Security Deposit Refund & Leave-and-License Disputes
jurisdiction: Pune District (and equivalent District/Small Causes Courts across Maharashtra)

contact_channels.offline_pune_anchor: District & Sessions Court / Small Causes Court, CTS No. 9 & 9A, FP No. 805 & 891, Shivajinagar, Pune – 411005

categories: Residential Leave & License possession/eviction (Competent Authority, Section 24 MRCA 1999)
Tenancies, commercial licenses, and monetary security deposit refund recovery (Court of Small Causes)
mandatory_pre_steps: Compile registered Leave & License Agreement (compulsory registration under Sec 55 MRCA 1999), deposit transfer proof, key handover proof, and move-out photos.
Send a formal 15-day written Demand Notice via email and Registered Speed Post.
Attempt free pre-litigation advice via Tele-Law or pre-litigation mediation/Lok Adalat via DLSA Pune.
exclusions: Do not file pure civil security deposit recovery as a police complaint unless distinct criminal cheating/fraud occurred (e.g., forged ownership or concealed bank seizure).
documents_required: Registered Leave & License Agreement
UPI/NEFT/cheque proof of security deposit payment
Move-out inspection / timestamped condition photos & key handover confirmation
Paid electricity/society maintenance receipts
Copy of 15-day Demand Notice and postal tracking receipt
step_by_step_guide: Gather agreement, deposit payment proof, utility clearance, and move-out photos.
Send a 15-day written Demand Notice to the landlord via email + Registered Speed Post.
Book a free Tele-Law call or approach DLSA Pune for pre-litigation Lok Adalat/mediation (and free lawyer if Sec 12 eligible).
If unresolved, file a recovery suit in the Court of Small Causes, Shivajinagar, Pune.
escalation_path: 15-Day Demand Notice -> Tele-Law / DLSA Pre-Litigation Lok Adalat -> Court of Small Causes, Pune.

automation.recommended_handoff: 15-Day Security Deposit Demand Notice PDF generator + move-out evidence checklist + DLSA/Tele-Law bridge.
